description: List observatories whose telescope share is above the average share, ordered by how far above average they are. Return the top 10 plus every observatory tied with the 10th on that difference.

c.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and work out its share of all telescopes (its count divided by the total number of telescopes). Which are the top 10 observatories whose share is above the average share across observatories, ranked by how far above average they are? Show the `observstation`, the telescope count, the share, and the share minus the average share, unrounded, from the biggest gap to the smallest. List observatories whose telescope share is above the average share, ordered by how far above average they are. Return the top 10 plus every observatory tied with the 10th on that difference.
c.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, CAST(telescope_count AS REAL) / NULLIF(SUM(telescope_count) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM station_counts), differences AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_minus_average FROM shares), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share_minus_average DESC) AS position FROM differences WHERE share_minus_average > 0) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share_minus_average FROM ranked WHERE position <= 10 ORDER BY share_minus_average DESC, observstation;

b.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and divide by the total number of telescopes; compute the average of these shares across all observatories, then return those above the average, ordered by share minus average share descending, including the top 10 and every observatory tied for 10th, with `observstation`, telescope count, share, and unrounded difference
b.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, 1.0 * telescope_count / NULLIF(SUM(telescope_count) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM station_counts), differences AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference FROM shares), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY difference DESC) AS position FROM differences) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, difference FROM ranked WHERE difference > 0 AND position <= 10 ORDER BY difference DESC, observstation;

a.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and work out its share of all telescopes (its count divided by the total number of telescopes). Among observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, list the `observstation`, the telescope count, the share, and how far the share is above the average (share minus average share), with no rounding. Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return the top 10, also including every observatory that ties with the 10th one on that difference, even if that means more than 10 rows.
a.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, telescope_count * 1.0 / SUM(telescope_count) OVER () AS share FROM station_counts), compared AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference_above_average FROM shares), ranked AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, difference_above_average, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY difference_above_average DESC) AS position FROM compared WHERE difference_above_average > 0) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, difference_above_average FROM ranked WHERE position <= 10 ORDER BY difference_above_average DESC, observstation;

d.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and calculate its share of all telescopes (its count divided by the total telescope count). Find the observatories whose share exceeds the average share across observatories, ranked by share minus average share from largest to smallest. Return the top 10 plus all observatories tied with the 10th, showing `observstation`, telescope count, share, and share minus average share, with values unrounded.
d.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, telescope_count * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(telescope_count) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM station_counts), deviations AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_minus_average_share FROM shares), ranked AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share_minus_average_share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share_minus_average_share DESC) AS share_rank FROM deviations WHERE share_minus_average_share > 0) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share_minus_average_share FROM ranked WHERE share_rank <= 10 ORDER BY share_minus_average_share DESC, observstation;
